summary.text: Greg Landsman is the Democratic U.S. Representative for Ohio's 1st District and won re-election on November 3, 2026, according to unofficial results. A Cincinnati native who worked in education nonprofits and state government and served on the Cincinnati City Council before his 2022 election to Congress, he serves on the Energy and Commerce Committee.

paragraphs.text: Landsman was born in Cincinnati in 1976 and lives in Mt. Washington, Ohio.
He earned a B.A. in economics and political science from Ohio University in 1999 and an M.A. in theological studies, religion, and public policy from Harvard University in 2004.
He describes himself as a former teacher and the son of teachers who spent most of his career working on behalf of children and families.
Landsman worked as executive director of The Strive Partnership with the KnowledgeWorks Foundation and as director of the Ohio Governor's Office of Faith-Based and Community Initiatives.
According to his congressional biography, he led a ballot measure to make Cincinnati the first city in America to provide two years of preschool.

He served on the Cincinnati City Council from 2018 to 2022, and the same biography cites his work on eviction prevention reforms and investments in prenatal care, child care, affordable housing and youth jobs.
Landsman was elected to the U.S. House in 2022, succeeding Steve Chabot, and took office in January 2023.

He serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee, including its Health, Communications and Technology, and Environment subcommittees, co-chairs the bipartisan What Works Caucus and co-founded the Lowering Costs Caucus.
According to his congressional biography, he lives in Cincinnati with his wife, Sarah, and their two children.
He won the November 3, 2026 general election with 54.4% of the vote to Eric Conroy's 42.9% and Nathan Weise's 2.7%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
